newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude sharply off on heat losses, technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude sharply off on heat losses, technicals.

text.p: NYMEX crude declined sharply Tuesday afternoon hit by technical selling and caught in heating oil's downdraft, traders said.
"Once it fell below $25.00 there were a lot of stops set off. It has sort of fed on itself after that," said a trader.
At 1447 EST, January crude was off 82 cents at $24.48 a barrel after falling as low as $24.28.

"A lot of this is weather related. The forecast was orginally for cold, and now it's going to be warmer," said Al Lindseth, trader with GSC Energy. January heating oil was off 2.33 cents at 69.80 cents a gallon.
The National Weather Service's six to 10 day outlook released Monday called for above normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.

January gasoline was off 1.98 cents at 66.90 cents a gallon. Traders were anticipating a build in refined product stocks in weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) expected out Tuesday evening.
"There is little talk of the APIs. People are letting loose because we no longer have the weather or uncertainty about Iraq supporting prices," said a trader.
Traders also said the market was now facing the reality of Iraq's resuming crude exports following news that United Nations was receiving oil contracts from Iraq under the oil-for-food plan.
"The market is getting spooked by the deal now," said a dealer.

On Monday, U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali gave final clearance for a deal which eases sanctions against Iraq and allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, in exchange for humanitarian aid.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
